The project duration is 30 months, divided into three 10-month phases for foundational research, model development, and validation/deployment preparation.
Dr. Anya Sharma, Principal Investigator in Computer Science, leads the project.
Key stakeholders are Local Utility Companies' Operations & Planning groups and the Environmental Protection Agency's Climate Modeling Division.

Objectives include identifying key climate-related drivers of energy demand fluctuations, publishing at least two high-impact research papers, and providing actionable insights and scenario planning tools for regional energy agencies to enhance grid stability and resource allocation.

Deliverables include an open-source repository for the models and scripts, interactive visualization tools for model outputs, validated predictive models demonstrating improved accuracy, and a technical report detailing methodology, results, and recommendations for operational implementation.

The project will anonymize and aggregate potentially sensitive energy consumption data, follow strict data privacy protocols, consider societal impacts, maintain transparency, and avoid biases in predictive model applications.
